title: Design System: Next In Research — The Library Record

display.purpose: The front-page h1 across the 12-column measure (at lg sized 5cqi to its column: always two full-width lines), and the closing 'Back Cohort Two.' Bricolage 800 on flame.

headline.purpose: Section and page openers; nothing floats above them.

numeral.purpose: Flame figures inside the By-the-numbers catalog card.

body.purpose: Public Sans prose; the front-page mission deck runs 1.125–1.25rem, then at lg a single full-measure line sized 2.36cqi to its column, with an 'Our mission:' run-in.

label.purpose: Courier uppercase printed parts of objects and chrome: dateline strip, card and sheet headers, chips, subnav tabs, table heads.

data.purpose: Courier facts: call numbers, dates, bylines, cutlines, credits, ledger labels.

scale.purpose: The enumerated fixed size steps (typography.scale in DESIGN.md frontmatter): Courier labels and data at 10–15px, Public Sans body 16px with leads and decks at 18–20px, Bricolage titles, headlines, statements, numerals, and banners from 1.5rem to 4.5rem. The front-page banner (5cqi) and deck (2.36cqi) are column-sized at lg.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow of cards, press cards, tables, albums, gallery thumbnails.

shadows.name: print
shadows.purpose: Archival prints, portrait mounts, and the hover state of clickable photographs.

shadows.name: print-lg
shadows.purpose: A band's single hero object (front-page photo mount, By-the-numbers card, circulation sheet, hold slip, ledger); hover of press and contact cards; the photo in the lightbox.

shadows.name: nav-scrolled

motion.name: stamp-in

motion.name: photo-lift
motion.purpose: Hover on straight press photographs: Top 10 spread and GalleryThumb.

narrative.overview:
The site is a public library's own record of a finished summer, and since September 2026 that record opens as a front page. Flame-orange fields (user-pinned, Aug 2026) open and close it like a broadsheet pasted to the library door. Buckram-cloth green is the institution's furniture: the nav bar and its archive menu, the vision band, the photo viewer, and the footer. Between the two, clean paper neutrals carry the evidence as physical objects: catalog cards, a circulation sheet, an accession ledger, a hold slip, and, new with the Front Page, straight press photographs with white keylines and typed cutlines. Evidence is the aesthetic. A date is stamped, a mentor is filed under a call number, a photograph carries its credit. The world still refuses both the dark SaaS gradient hero and the sterile white nonprofit template (world contract seed 1ec49fef), and the home contract (seed afe8fa7a, first comment in `<body>` of `index.html`) adds a third refusal: the stat-tile SaaS hero.

The mood is civic, proud, and matter-of-fact: a well-run county institution reporting what happened. Density is generous but orderly. A flame band announces, paper bands present the evidence, cloth does the bookkeeping. Two photographic registers coexist: *press photographs* (the home page and every gallery) sit straight in thin white keylines, like prints on a newspaper page, while *archival prints* on the archive's interior pages still rest slightly tilted as if just set down. Typography splits into three voices: poster capitals for announcements, plain civic sans for talking to families, and typewriter mono for anything a librarian would type, stamp, or caption.
keyCharacteristics: Two colored registers over one paper ground: flame announces (front page, close, primary buttons, headline numerals), cloth administers (nav, archive menu, vision band, photo viewer, footer). Never a plain white page.
Clean paper neutrals (#F3F1EC family) as the card stock; the warm manila rendition is retired.
Ephemera as components: catalog cards, the By-the-numbers card, the circulation sheet, the accession ledger, the hold slip, rod holes, and press photographs with Courier cutlines.
Two stamp inks carry all status: red for what happened, blue for what is pending.
Strictly rectilinear edges; the only circles are drilled holes and dots.
One authored motion: things arrive the way a rubber stamp lands.
A single light world with no dark mode; the cloth greens are the dark register.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Flame announces, cloth administers. Flame fields open and close the home page and fill the primary action on paper; cloth is the institution's furniture: nav, archive menu, vision band, photo viewer, footer. Paper bands carry the evidence between them. Neither register grounds a whole interior page; those are paper.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Status is always a stamp, and the ink states the tense: red for what happened (HELD, a stamped date), blue for what is pending (DUE, HOLD FOR, in processing). No green, amber, or gray status pills exist in this world.

rules.name: The Card, Not Page Rule
rules.body: Paper-bright surfaces are always bounded objects (bordered in paper-shade, ink-shadowed, often rod-holed) sitting on a paper, cloth, or flame field. There is no edge-to-edge white or off-white page.

rules.name: The Typed Data Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is reserved for what a librarian or a news desk would type: identifiers, dates, bylines, cutlines, credits, statuses, labels, and the contents of catalog cards. It never sets narrative prose paragraphs or display headings.

rules.name: The Run-In Rule
rules.body: The program's two standing statements are set as run-ins, never as labels: "Our mission:" in bold paper-bright leading the front-page deck, and "Our vision:" in Bricolage 800 opening the cloth band's h2 (the rest of that heading in 600). The lead-in belongs to the sentence it starts.

rules.name: The No Floating Label Rule
rules.body: Small mono labels exist only as printed parts of objects (a card's header, a sheet's caption, a slip's hold line) or as the front page's dateline strip, which spans the full measure between two paper-bright/40 rules and carries only typed facts (cohort, date, place, "Free for every family"). No eyebrow or kicker label floats above a section heading.

rules.name: The Ink-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are diffuse, downward, and ink-tinted. Elevation is reserved: `card` at rest, `print` for photographs, `print-lg` only for a band's single hero object. Hover may step one level (`card` → `print` on photographs, `card` → `print-lg` on press and contact cards) but never invents a new shadow.

rules.name: The Guillotine Rule
rules.body: Corners are square because paper is cut, not molded. The only permitted circles are holes and dots. Rounding anything else breaks the material.

rules.name: The Press-Print Rule
rules.body: A photograph that reports (home, galleries, the viewer) is straight and keylined in white; a photograph that is kept (the archive's standalone prints) may tilt. Never tilt a press photograph, and never frame one with anything but white.

dos: **Do** keep the two registers straight: flame grounds the front page, the close, and primary buttons; cloth grounds the chrome (nav, archive menu, vision band, viewer, footer); paper grounds content. Seam the flame front page to paper with an 8px flame-deep rule and paper to paper with an `ink/10` hairline.

**Do** set press photographs straight in a white keyline (8px on the lead, 4px on thumbnails) with a Courier cutline and, on the lead, the photo credit. Hover lifts `card` → `print` and fades the image to 90%.
**Do** reserve tilt for kept objects: archival `PhotoPrint`s on interior archive pages and the hold slip, at −1.4° to +1.6°, straightening on hover.
**Do** carry status with stamps in the right ink (red happened, blue pending) using the double-ring `Stamp` and its spring (stiffness 420, damping 21). One stamp per first viewport.
**Do** build figure boxes as catalog cards: red-rule margin, paper-shade border, rod hole, Courier labels, flame Bricolage numerals.
**Do** open every Cohort One archive page with `CohortSubnav`, and route every internal link through `PageLink` so it is a real anchor.
**Do** give every photo gallery the `Lightbox`: counter, arrow keys, swipe, Escape, focus trap, and focus return.
**Do** size thumbnails from the photo's own width and height so masonry never jumps.
**Do** honor reduced motion at both layers: `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` and the global CSS kill switch.
**Do** keep Courier Prime for typed data, labels, bylines, and cutlines; Public Sans for prose; Bricolage for headings and numerals. Three voices, never swapped.
**Do** limit icons to functional lucide strokes (arrows, chevrons, mail, external-link, menu, X) at 16–20px.
donts: **Don't** round a corner. Only rod holes and dot markers are circles (The Guillotine Rule).
**Don't** tilt a press photograph or frame one in anything but white (The Press-Print Rule).
**Don't** warm the neutrals back toward manila or cream. The card stock is the clean paper trio (#F3F1EC / #FDFCFA / #E1DED6).
**Don't** set flame-bright (#EE6C4D) as text or on paper; it is a small dot on cloth-deep only.
**Don't** float eyebrow or kicker labels above headings. Mono labels belong inside objects, and the only strip above a heading is the front-page dateline between rules.
**Don't** lay out figures as bare stat tiles; numbers live inside a catalog-card box or a dot-leader ledger.
**Don't** introduce a dark mode or new dark surfaces; the cloth greens are this light world's entire dark register.
**Don't** author new entrance animations. The stamp-in spring is the only arrival; everything else is a functional fade, reveal, lift, or straighten at 160–300ms.
**Don't** use pure-black or colored shadows; every shadow tints from catalog ink or deep cloth.
**Don't** let transformed objects widen the page; `overflow-x: clip` on `html`/`body` is load-bearing.
**Don't** name students in captions, cutlines, or alt text; captions name the research, not the researcher.
